Jordan / Kimberly — attaching the files I ran yesterday against a mirrored Dedicated pool. Highlights:

- Isolation approach: we use customer-to-pool affinity + GPU reservation at the hypervisor/runtime boundary. For NVIDIA-based nodes we enforce GPU device assignment (no vGPU multiplexing across customers) and disable CUDA MPS for multi-customer tenancy.
- Memory and KV cache: the inference runtime keeps per-session KV in an in-process heap mapped to the GPU address space. We never accept remote KV restoration from other customer sessions. The GPU memory allocations are freed on session termination; the allocator zeroes freed buffers before reuse.
- Eviction behavior: when a tenant exceeds its configured burst/slot limits we trigger a graceful preemption: active requests are routed to a warm fallback model hosted in a different pool while the evicted tenant's jobs are throttled. Eviction events and the fallback routing decision are recorded in node logs (example attached).
- NUMA / CPU pinning: we pin critical scheduler threads to the NUMA domain closest to the assigned GPU to minimize cross-node memory traffic; notes included in test-plan.

Attachments: node-eviction-trace-20261027.txt, isolation-test-plan.md

If you need a sanitized p99 trace (redacted IPs/job-ids) I can produce that; the attached trace is already trimmed to the eviction window.
